source.title: Good Pretraining, Bad SFT: Checkpoint Quality Across the Training Stack
source.authors: Sohir Maskey; Philipp Scholl; Jonas Knupp; Pit Neitemeier; Sascha Wirges

record.tranche_reason: Measures checkpoint performance retention under weight perturbations and compares it with post-training performance, but does not measure the train-test generalization gap named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports perturbation-retention results for three checkpoints on GSM8K and MBPP at two perturbation scales. It does not measure fitting random labels, training error versus test error, or the architecture, optimizer, batch-size, explicit-regularization, or model-size effects in V1–V8. Post-SFT scores are downstream benchmark performance, not train-test gaps.
record.test_reason: The study measures benchmark retention under isotropic Gaussian weight perturbations and performance after subsequent training. It does not test any listed version. In particular, its solution-density probe does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, training-error tolerance, or the train–test generalization gap required by V7. Its discussion of flatness and generalization provides background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Current checkpoint metrics can misrank sources for subsequent training; solution-density differences are consistent with downstream adaptability but establish neither causation nor general predictive validity. The large aggregate reversal is amplified by COOLDOWN's stopping and repetition failure.
record.recipe_differences: A 30B MoE language-model training pipeline and Gaussian weight-perturbation solution-density probe, rather than the image-classification generalization experiments in the listed originals.
record.method_sensitivity: Perturbation retention differs by checkpoint and benchmark; measured at σϵ = 0.005 and σϵ = 0.001.

fits_no_version.finding: Checkpoint-specific benchmark retention differs under Gaussian weight perturbations. At σ = 0.005, GSM8K retention at the 90% threshold is 27%, 0%, and 13% for CONSTANT, COOLDOWN, and MERGE. At σ = 0.001, MBPP mean retention is 99.7%, 95.2%, and 98.3%. The ordering is not universal: GSM8K mean retention places COOLDOWN slightly above MERGE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local benchmark-retention profiles distinguish these pretrained checkpoints and are broadly consistent with their downstream adaptability, without establishing a general predictor or causal relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: COOLDOWN improves pretraining loss and aggregate performance over CONSTANT but reaches a lower post-SFT aggregate after the same continuation: 0.247 versus 0.360. Excluding HumanEval+ shrinks the difference to 0.016.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Better current checkpoint metrics can fail to identify the best starting point for a fixed subsequent training pipeline.

record.problems: One 30B MoE family and one seed per setup; solution density measured on only two tasks; 100 perturbations per condition; the authors state that the measurement does not establish causation, and a single unperturbed evaluation makes values above 100% uncertain as local improvements.
record.rows_left_out: Post-SFT aggregate scores and stage correlations were not included as rows because they report pipeline-conditioned downstream benchmark performance, not a measure of the claim's train-test generalization gap. Other solution-density thresholds in Tables 11–12 were omitted to keep the extraction focused on the reported 90% threshold and mean retention.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on random versus natural labels.
Width increases beyond interpolation and their effects on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization regimes.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, training-error tolerance, correlation with train–test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. The supplied row values match Tables 11–12. The study explicitly distinguishes capability retention from pretraining-loss flatness. No omitted result tests V1–V8; downstream scores and additional thresholds are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Batch-size effects on train-test generalization gaps.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and train-test gap measurement; the study measures downstream score retention under Gaussian weight perturbations instead.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.operation_detail: Measured fraction of Gaussian weight perturbations retaining at least 90% of the checkpoint's unperturbed benchmark score.

rows.note: Perturbation retention is not a train-test gap measure.
rows.check: Value is correct. Baseline should specify the same checkpoint's unperturbed GSM8K score, whose absolute value is not reported; the threshold is 90% of that score.
